```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.4,
                      dpi = 110, out.width = "100%")
has_inla <- requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)
```

`bruce` turns scattered temperature readings from networks of very different
quality into daily maps for a whole city. This article walks through the full
workflow on a synthetic city, so every step can be checked against a known
truth.

Code that fits models needs R-INLA and is shown but not run when this page is
built; everything else runs.

## A synthetic city

`bruce_simulate()` invents a 30 km city with two hills, an urban core, 12
reference stations, 40 low-cost sensors that read 1.5 °C too warm, and a
coarse reanalysis-like background. It returns the "true" temperature on every
pixel, which real data never gives us.

```{r sim}
library(bruce)
sim <- bruce_simulate(n_reference = 12, n_biased = 40, n_days = 5, seed = 1)

head(sim$obs)
sim$sources
```

```{r sim-plot, fig.height = 3}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(2, 2, 3, 4))
terra::plot(sim$covariates$elev, main = "Elevation (m)",
            col = hcl.colors(50, "Terrain 2"))
terra::plot(sim$covariates$urb, main = "Urban fraction",
            col = hcl.colors(50, "Grays", rev = TRUE))
terra::plot(sim$truth[[3]], main = "True temperature, day 3",
            col = hcl.colors(50, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE))
ref <- sim$stations$source == "reference"
points(sim$stations$x, sim$stations$y, pch = ifelse(ref, 24, 21),
       bg = "white", cex = 0.7)
par(op)
```

## 1. Declare the data

Everything city-specific enters through one call. `sources` says which
networks are trusted (`bias = FALSE`) and which get an estimated offset, and
whether each network's noise is known (`obs_sd`) or estimated (`NA`).

```{r data}
d <- bruce_data(sim$obs, sim$stations, sim$sources, crs = sim$crs,
                background = sim$background)
d <- bruce_covariates(d, sim$covariates, background_buffer = 4500)
d
```

For a real city the same four objects come from your own databases: one row
per station and day in `obs`, coordinates in `stations`, and a small table
describing each network.

## 2. Mesh and specification

```{r mesh, eval = has_inla}
mesh <- bruce_mesh(d)
spec <- bruce_spec()   # defaults: range prior anchored on station spacing, collapse handling on
```

`bruce_spec()` holds every modelling decision: priors, whether to include the
station and daily terms, and what to do if the spatial field degenerates.

## 3. Fit

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
fit <- bruce_fit(d, mesh, spec, keep_config = TRUE)
summary(fit)
bruce_check(fit)   # each fitting attempt and whether the field collapsed
```

When the day-to-day correlation of the field drifts to 1 (a failure seen with
clustered sensor networks), `bruce_fit()` restarts the optimiser and, if
needed, refits with that correlation fixed. Every attempt is recorded.

## 4. Predict, decompose, aggregate

```{r use, eval = FALSE}
pred <- bruce_predict(fit, n_samples = 200, keep_samples = TRUE)
terra::plot(pred$mean[[3]])

dec <- bruce_decompose(fit)
plot(dec, date = "2025-01-03")   # total, covariate part, spatial field

zones <- sf::st_sf(zone = "city", geometry = sf::st_geometry(sim$domain))
bruce_zonal(pred, zones, "zone")
```

`bruce_decompose()` splits each day's surface into the part explained by
covariates and the spatial field learned from stations, and reports how much
of the spatial variance each carries, including their covariance.

## 5. Validate

```{r cv, eval = FALSE}
cv <- bruce_cv(d, mesh, spec, scheme = "lso", checkpoint_dir = "cv_lso")
cv
```

Leave-station-out (`"lso"`) removes one reference station per fold;
leave-region-out (`"lro"`) removes every station in a region, a harder test of
how the map behaves where there is no data. Each fold is saved as it finishes,
so long runs can be resumed.

## Using your own city

The only requirement is the data contract: daily values per station, station
coordinates with a network label, a table describing the networks, and
covariate rasters. An optional gridded product on the same variable (e.g.
ERA5-Land) can be added as background. `inst/examples/rio_adapter.R` shows the
mapping used for Rio de Janeiro.
